answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to anchor a verifiable work kernel whose output is bound to a stake that cannot be duplicated cheaply. New identities start with a glacier-slow reputation: transaction volume and trust limits thaw gradually only after a history of honest, settled exchanges. Meanwhile the network samples a pulse of random peer audits — cheap spot checks demanding proof of the original work — so one operator running thousands of fake agents pays the full cost of thousands of kernels plus audit risk on every one, while honest agents pay once.
